classification.difficultyReason: Recognise a critical point where the derivative is undefined and compare its value with both endpoint values.

content.prompt: Find the global minimum and maximum for $y=5-\sqrt[3]{(x-2)^2}$ in the domain $[-10,10]$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrowheads at both ends; blue curve with a pointed maximum and filled endpoints. Left endpoint below the horizontal axis; right endpoint above it.
spec.mathematics: y=5-|x-2|^(2/3) on [-10,10]; cusp at (2,5); endpoint values 5-cuberoot(144) and 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no answer coordinates or extrema labels.

answer.short: Global minimum at $\left(-10,5-\sqrt[3]{144}\right)$; global maximum at $(2,5)$.
answer.worked:
For $x\ne2$,
$$y'=-\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{x-2}}.$$
The derivative is never zero and is undefined at $x=2$, where the function is defined. Compare this point with the endpoints:
$$\begin{aligned}y(-10)&=5-\sqrt[3]{(-12)^2}\\&=5-\sqrt[3]{144}\\y(2)&=5\\y(10)&=5-\sqrt[3]{8^2}\\&=1\end{aligned}$$
Since $\sqrt[3]{144}>5$, the smallest value is $5-\sqrt[3]{144}$ and the largest is $5$.
The global minimum is at $\left(-10,5-\sqrt[3]{144}\right)$ and the global maximum is at $(2,5)$.
